findings.finding: Opens 'We did not replicate three of the four simulation headline findings of Chen (2021), who reported that ...' and names the three failed headlines (biased natural direct effects, under-covering percentile bootstrap CIs, near-zero mediated-interaction power) with paired published-vs-ours numbers: 85.42 vs 0.00 (% direct-effect results with |bias| > .10), 43.62 vs 0.04 (coverage shortfall), 47.07 vs 0.33 (imbalance), near zero vs 0.836 (MINT power, n = 500, a = .59, h = .34). Verdict, citation and original finding are in one sentence, as required.

Limit of the evidence follows immediately: cause not established because Chen's comparison step and result files are unavailable; HSIS comparison not established for lack of data (blocked, not called a nonreplication).

Fourth headline gets its own verdict ('Her tentative minimum n of 5,000 was partly replicated: 86.3% ... and 89.2% ...'), matching REPLICATION-PLAN.yaml hl-n5000 'partly'. Polish: '29 of her 44 tested Type I and power statements agree' does not say 'with our run' and reads as if she tested them; the abstract itself does not state the tolerance (the Table 1 caption on page 1 does).

Repeats the verdict first with exact counts ('all 3,840 of 3,840 condition-cutoff cells') and the four headline pairs, quoting 'All power for MINT is near zero' (verified verbatim at PDF p. 135 = printed p. 121).

Then the limit (cause not established; HSIS blocked), then the direction statement ('No headline effect reversed its sign ... about 140 times (imbalance) and over 1,000 times (shortfall) smaller'; recomputed 47.07/0.326 = 144, 43.62/0.036 = 1218), then the tolerance ('half a unit in Chen's last printed decimal ... 0.005, 0.005 and 0.01 percentage points; ... not a sampling band').

'and 39 would hold if our cells are read with h replaced by 0, a reading of our results rather than a test of her runs' is unexplained at this point and only intelligible after Section 5.2 (p. 8); it is hedged and not a buried verdict, so polish only.
Defines PNIE/TNIE/PNDE/TNDE/MINT, 'condition-cutoff cell' and 'both-zero products' on page 1; RDD, CI, HSIS defined on p. 2.
'Slack' and 'If h = 0' columns are defined in the caption; the linked file name is broken mid-word as 'statement_chec ks.csv' (polish).
Reads 'qualitative sample-size recommendation over the grid. A qualitative design recommendation over the whole grid; ...' - repetitive, lowercase start, reads as machine-filled (polish).

FAIL: the sentence-level accounting of Chen's Type I and power sections is not complete, contrary to the paper's presentation ('44 Type I and power statements are tested and six sentences excluded'). Reading PDF pp. 113-135 sentence by sentence, two result-bearing sentences are neither among the 44 tested statements nor among the six exclusions: (i) PDF p. 126 (printed 112): 'The corresponding TNIE2 and TNIE3 power results across levels of a, b, and h are not displayed because of their similarity in overall patterns to the TNIE1 results' - a cutoff-similarity claim that is checkable and substantive in our run (e.g. TNIE a = .39, b = 0, h = .15, n = 1,000: power .940/.850/.564 at cutoffs 1/2/3; 38 of 225 TNIE nonzero cell-set-by-n combinations have a cutoff spread > .05 under the script's own 'no differences' reading); (ii) PDF p. 132 (printed 118): 'Power results for TNDE2 and TNDE3 ... are not shown because the overall patterns were similar to TNDE1 results' (only partly covered by statement 42, which is restricted to h = .15). A lesser case: PDF p. 120 (printed 106) 'Further, the Type I error rates were close to the targeted .05' (TNDE) is absent from statement 14's wording although statement 12 carries the same phrase for PNDE. Each must be tested or listed in Table 8 with a reason; all other sentences on pp. 113-135 are tested, listed as excluded, or plainly method/figure description.
